newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia ratifies U.N. drugs convention.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia ratifies U.N. drugs convention.

text.p: The Indonesian parliament has ratified a 1971 United Nations convention on the use of psychotropic drugs, the official Antara news agency said on Tuesday.

Indonesian Health Minister Sujudi was quoted as saying that the aim of the convention was to prevent the abuse of psychotropic substances, such as the designer drug Ecstasy, and to protect their use in the medical profession.
"The convention is also aimed at safeguarding the use of psychotropic substances in the medical field and at protecting their producers," Sujudi said.
Indonesia is currently preparing a law to ban trade in, and use of, Ecstasy.
The Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Tuesday that customs and excise authorities at Bali's Ngurah Rai Airport found 29,295 Ecstasy pills in two suitcases left unclaimed for three months.
The suitcases had arrived on a flight which originated in Amsterdam, it said.
